structure.title: Seeking a place
structure.text: Oedipus arrives as a vulnerable stranger and must negotiate whether he can remain on sacred ground.

structure.title: Competing claims
structure.text: Family and political visitors approach him with conflicting demands. Questions of protection and consent organise the encounters.

people.name: Oedipus
people.text: Old, blind and long banished from Thebes, he arrives on sacred ground outside Athens and refuses to move, sure this is where his wandering is meant to end.

people.name: Antigone
people.text: His daughter, who has guided him on the road for years, and who is torn between her father and the brothers fighting over Thebes.

people.name: Theseus
people.text: The king of Athens, asked to shelter a polluted stranger whom Thebes now wants back, and who must decide what hospitality and honour require.

context.title: Earlier catastrophe
context.text: Oedipus has lost his kingship and discovered devastating truths about his family. The play begins with the person who must continue living afterwards.

context.title: Sanctuary
context.text: Sacred places and promises of protection can constrain political action. A vulnerable visitor may possess claims that force rulers to answer him.
context.takeaway: Weakness does not erase all authority.

notice.why: Visitors reveal what they value through the terms they offer.
Suffering and culpability are being reconsidered.

opening: An old blind man arrives outside Athens with his daughter, looking for somewhere he can sit without being driven away. His name is Oedipus, and the people who hear it want him gone. Yet the exile whom nobody wishes to shelter is suddenly valuable to the rulers who once abandoned him. Sophocles returns to a ruined king whose remaining power lies in deciding whom to trust, and who refuses to let other people turn his suffering into an asset without his consent.
